history.summary: A D05 unit at One-North/Buona Vista, 510m from the EW21 Buona Vista MRT interchange, listed at $1,605 psf — ~10% below the $1,792 URA median. Anchored to the One-North research/tech employment hub with steady 5.3% resale CAGR. Smaller 334-unit development is the main liquidity caveat, but location quality earns a Buy.
history.rating_rationale: Location is the thesis: 510m to Buona Vista MRT (EW/CC interchange) directly serving the One-North research, biomedical and tech employment cluster plus NUS/Star Vista — a deep, durable tenant catchment that supports rent and resale. $1,605 psf is ~10% under the $1,792 median, a fair-to-good entry for D05 RCR. 5.3% resale CAGR (114 txns) is reliable. Caveats: only 334 units (smaller, thinner resale than the mega-developments here) and UEL is a mid-tier developer; reviews note in-block renovation noise and modest facilities. On balance the employment-anchored location and median discount outweigh these.
red_flags: Smaller 334-unit development — shallower resale liquidity than 600+ unit peers
Mid-tier developer (UEL); reviews cite frequent renovation noise and basic facilities
5.3% CAGR is solid but the lowest growth rate among the D19 value plays here
catalysts: 510m to Buona Vista MRT interchange feeding One-North jobs hub + NUS — durable tenant demand
One-North continued expansion (biomedical/tech/Fusionopolis) deepens the catchment
~10% discount to URA median provides entry margin

history.summary: 1BR loft (1,022 sqft, double-volume) at Buona Vista, D5/RCR, asking $1,468 PSF — genuinely below the project's ~$1,535 PSF 6-month average and a directly comparable 1,023 sqft loft listing at $1,564 PSF. The bedroom_sqft_mismatch flag is a FALSE alarm: 1,022 sqft is a real Rochester 1BR loft layout, not a mislabel.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,500,000 ($1,468 PSF) sits below the verified 6-month transacted average of ~$1,535 PSF and below a comparable 1,023 sqft 1BR loft asking $1,600,000/$1,564 PSF (PropNex), so the algo's age_adj_premium of -14.5% reflects a real discount, not a quirk — appreciation_txns=114 and the 177-txn project history give a deep, trustworthy comp base. Location is the catalyst: ~5 min walk to Buona Vista interchange (EWL + Circle Line) and the one-north tech/biomed employment cluster, supporting both rental demand (project shows 1,511 rental txns, rents $4.1k-$11k) and resale liquidity. D5 is RCR, which the v3.4 backtest prior favors over CCR for forward returns. Held back from Strong Buy by the loft format (high ceilings = lower usable yield per dollar than a flat 1BR), 99-yr lease aging from 2011 TOP, and psf_cohort_txns of only 5 for this specific loft band.
red_flags: 1BR loft format priced like a 2BR ($1.5M outlay for one bedroom) compresses rental yield vs a conventional 1BR
99-yr leasehold, ~14 yrs elapsed (TOP 2011) — lease decay accelerates over a 5-7yr hold horizon
psf_cohort_txns only 5 for the loft size band — fewer same-size comps than the 114 project-wide figure implies
catalysts: 5-min walk to Buona Vista MRT interchange (East-West + Circle Line)
one-north / Fusionopolis tech-biomed employment cluster underpins tenant demand and exit liquidity
RCR location aligns with v3.4 prior favoring RCR/OCR forward returns over CCR

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Strong rental backbone: 1,511 rental transactions to date, asking rents $4,100-$11,000; tenant pool from one-north and NUS/biopolis. But the ~$1.5M price for a single-bedroom loft caps gross yield around 3.3-3.6%, mid-pack for D5.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: URA 5yr CAGR 5.33% on 114 txns is robust by sample size but per v3.4 has ~0 forward predictive power — do not extrapolate. Forward case rests on verified value (cheap vs real comps) plus the durable one-north/interchange catalyst, not trailing momentum.
